input.summary:
Roofs part (parts/roofs.mjs) now lays with no OFF-PALETTE and no REFUSED writes; make.sh exits 0 and writes build.nbt.
Off-palette fixes: bungalow verge (quartz) became smooth_quartz (quartz_slab x12 gone); boarding-house gable ends use polished_tuff (tuff_bricks x18 gone); smooth_quartz_stairs are swapped to quartz_stairs at write time through a proxy (the roof takes one material name for stairs and slabs).
Side changes: the I-house verge is smooth_quartz, the plan's spelling (it was not reported off-palette before). The "kept N cells" lines are the plan's keep boxes, not refusals; the part report shows refused 0.
left: Remaining OFF-PALETTE line in make.sh is from roof.json (the dogtrot roof, laid by runParts after the shell): cut_copper x3, cut_copper_stairs x17, cut_copper_slab x3. It is not in parts/roofs.mjs, so I left it; the fix is exposed_cut_copper in roof.json, owned by the shell or roof spec.
The boarding-house gable ends are polished_tuff, a substitute for tuff_bricks; the stairs and slabs stay tuff_brick_stairs and tuff_brick_slab. Check the look against the plan's olive-grey intent.
The bungalow verge stairs are quartz_stairs (written as the palette stand-in for smooth_quartz_stairs). Its slabs are smooth_quartz_slab, so the verge is one quartz family.

waste.what: Finding which cells carried each off-palette block: I dumped every part's cells by hand with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and filtered JSON to see that quartz_slab was on the bungalow, not the I-house, and that tuff_bricks sat on the boarding-house gable ends. The report only gives counts.
waste.cost: about 4 make.sh runs and 3 probe dumps of ~4000 cells each; roughly 25 minutes of wrong guesses (I first edited the I-house verge, which was not the culprit)
waste.tool: make.sh / build.mjs report should list OFF-PALETTE and REFUSED with x,y,z and the block (as the REFUSED line already does), and say which earlier-part or roof() call wrote it. MCD_PARTS_CELLS should be documented as the way to find them.

waste.what: Working out that roof() takes one material name for stairs, slabs and full blocks, so a verge whose slab and stair forms differ in the palette cannot be fixed by name. I had to write a write-time proxy to swap smooth_quartz_stairs to quartz_stairs.
waste.cost: 2 extra build runs and one proxy written by hand; the roof() materialAt hook did not affect the gable path
waste.tool: roof() option such as palette: palette.json (or a per-form map like {stairs, slab, full}) that picks the palette-valid form of each role; the library could expose a palette-aware material resolver. The materialAt hook could be documented as covering full blocks only where the gable path doesn't use it.

waste.what: Telling the keep-box cells apart from refused writes: the roof() log prints 'kept N cells' for both keep boxes and protected cells, which is confusing when a REFUSED line is what the owner asked me to clear.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of arithmetic on the camel hump keep (18 = 6x3 cells)
waste.tool: roof() should log keep-box exclusions and protect refusals separately, and the part report should carry them.

companions.task: Look at the boarding house gable ends (polished_tuff standing in for tuff_bricks) and the bungalow quartz verge, and say whether the tones read as the plan's olive-grey tin and white trim.

Off-palette fixes: bungalow verge (quartz) became smooth_quartz (quartz_slab x12 gone); boarding-house gable ends use polished_tuff (tuff_bricks x18 gone); smooth_quartz_stairs are swapped to quartz_stairs at write time through a proxy (the roof takes one material name for stairs and slabs).
Side changes: the I-house verge is smooth_quartz, the plan's spelling (it was not reported off-palette before). The "kept N cells" lines are the plan's keep boxes, not refusals; the part report shows refused 0.
left: Remaining OFF-PALETTE line in make.sh is from roof.json (the dogtrot roof, laid by runParts after the shell): cut_copper x3, cut_copper_stairs x17, cut_copper_slab x3. It is not in parts/roofs.mjs, so I left it; the fix is exposed_cut_copper in roof.json, owned by the shell or roof spec.
The boarding-house gable ends are polished_tuff, a substitute for tuff_bricks; the stairs and slabs stay tuff_brick_stairs and tuff_brick_slab. Check the look against the plan's olive-grey intent.
The bungalow verge stairs are quartz_stairs (written as the palette stand-in for smooth_quartz_stairs). Its slabs are smooth_quartz_slab, so the verge is one quartz family.

waste.what: Finding which cells carried each off-palette block: I dumped every part's cells by hand with MCD_PARTS_CELLS and filtered JSON to see that quartz_slab was on the bungalow, not the I-house, and that tuff_bricks sat on the boarding-house gable ends. The report only gives counts.
waste.cost: about 4 make.sh runs and 3 probe dumps of ~4000 cells each; roughly 25 minutes of wrong guesses (I first edited the I-house verge, which was not the culprit)
waste.tool: make.sh / build.mjs report should list OFF-PALETTE and REFUSED with x,y,z and the block (as the REFUSED line already does), and say which earlier-part or roof() call wrote it. MCD_PARTS_CELLS should be documented as the way to find them.

waste.what: Working out that roof() takes one material name for stairs, slabs and full blocks, so a verge whose slab and stair forms differ in the palette cannot be fixed by name. I had to write a write-time proxy to swap smooth_quartz_stairs to quartz_stairs.
waste.cost: 2 extra build runs and one proxy written by hand; the roof() materialAt hook did not affect the gable path
waste.tool: roof() option such as palette: palette.json (or a per-form map like {stairs, slab, full}) that picks the palette-valid form of each role; the library could expose a palette-aware material resolver. The materialAt hook could be documented as covering full blocks only where the gable path doesn't use it.

waste.what: Telling the keep-box cells apart from refused writes: the roof() log prints 'kept N cells' for both keep boxes and protected cells, which is confusing when a REFUSED line is what the owner asked me to clear.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of arithmetic on the camel hump keep (18 = 6x3 cells)
waste.tool: roof() should log keep-box exclusions and protect refusals separately, and the part report should carry them.

companions.task: Look at the boarding house gable ends (polished_tuff standing in for tuff_bricks) and the bungalow quartz verge, and say whether the tones read as the plan's olive-grey tin and white trim.
